letters.desc: ATC supports new NERC reliability standards and registration categories for large loads with pronounced oscillatory characteristics. ATC asks that any new standards be limited to loads meeting the behavior-based threshold so requirements remain targeted.
quotes: ATC strongly supports the implementation of robust operational standards for large load interconnections, particularly those exhibiting significant oscillatory behavior, because such behavior can cause voltage and frequency instability if not properly managed.

letters.desc: CAISO recommends NERC develop modeling and performance reliability standards specific to large loads, analogous to the MOD, PRC, and BAL standards that apply to large generators, to ensure consistent treatment across balancing authorities.
quotes: NERC should consider developing specific modeling and performance reliability standards for large loads, similar to MOD, PRC, and BAL standards applicable to large generators.

letters.org: North Carolina Utilities Commission Public Staff
letters.desc: The Public Staff agrees all NERC reliability standards must be met and notes NERC's Large Loads Task Force is nearing completion of draft guidelines. It argues issuing final rules before those guidelines are finalized would be counterproductive.
quotes: issuing final rules prior to those guidelines being finalized would be counterproductive.

letters.desc: ODEC endorses NERC's request that the Final Rule affirm NERC's full authority over the bulk power system, and calls for FERC to direct NERC to complete stakeholder coordination on registry criteria and reliability standard updates for large loads within one year of rule issuance.
quotes: ODEC reiterates its agreement with ANOPR Principle 14 and urges the Commission to adopt a requirement in the Final Rule that utilities serving large loads must meet all applicable NERC reliability standards and OATT provisions, as well as require large loads to be registered with NERC and require NERC to enhance its existing registry criteria and Reliability Standards and create new Standards as required to address the operational complexities that large loads introduce to the grid.
ODEC supports NERC's request that the Final Rule reflect the full scope of NERC's reliability authority as pertaining to the BPS.

letters.org: Pennsylvania Office of Consumer AdvocateDelaware Division of the Public Advocate
letters.desc: The filers support requiring all utilities and PJM to abide by NERC Reliability Standards and guidelines for large load interconnection, and ask that any deviations be disclosed to stakeholders with an explanation.
quotes: The interconnection study process should comply with all NERC guidelines and Reliability Standards and not be accelerated at the expense of reliability or accuracy of identifying network upgrades.

letters.desc: SMA asserts that its grid-forming inverter and BESS products already meet NERC reliability standards and OATT provisions, positioning them as ready-to-deploy solutions under any new FERC reliability requirements.
quotes: High performance grid-forming inverters are fully aligned with these requirements. For example, all of SMA's BESS solutions routinely meet applicable NERC reliability standards and OATT provisions, providing reliable support for consultants and system operators.

letters.desc: FirstEnergy argues that NERC TPL-001 and PRC-012-2 together require separate contingency testing of load and generation and require evaluating protection system failures. Netting short-circuits both requirements and conflicts with ANOPR principle fourteen.
quotes: Studying the net impact of hybrid facilities undermines the North American Electric Reliability Corporation ("NERC") transmission planning performance standards, which require testing the ability of the transmission system to withstand specific contingencies including loss of load and loss of generation.

if the transmission network is only planned to support the net withdrawal and export at the point of interconnection, the interconnection capability may be undersized compared to the amount of generation that could be made available at a time when the load customer is curtailed or not consuming power.
Protective equipment that would enforce a net amount is not a failsafe; to the contrary, such equipment suffers from an approximately 6% failure rate.
contingencies and control failures routinely defeat netting.
netting raises another issue not addressed in the initial comments: it undermines NERC standards and therefore also clashes with the ANOPR's principle fourteen.
